issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class defines a getter named getIngredientName(), while the solution's StockIngredient uses getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify exact getter names. This inconsistency between template and solution (different getter names) can confuse students comparing their work with the reference solution or when they try to follow the solution's code.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent getter name across template and solution. Either rename the template getter to getName() and update any references (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) or change the solution to use getIngredientName(). Also, update the problem statement to explicitly specify the expected getter names to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient 'name' field is named getIngredientName() in the template code but getName() in the solution. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual property (the ingredient's name) across artifacts can confuse students when they try to map the problem requirement to the provided code and to the reference solution—especially since Meal uses getName(). The problem statement requests adding getters for private fields but does not prescribe the exact getter name, so the mismatch between template and solution is an unintended naming inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single, consistent getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across all artifacts (preferably getName() to match Meal.getName()). Update the template's StockIngredient to provide getName(), and update any calls (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to use getName(), or alternatively change the solution to use getIngredientName() everywhere—ensuring template, solution, and instructions consistently reference the same identifier.
